ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act regulations, Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the OFAC SDN List (for USD clearing and correspondent-bank risk), FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons, and publicly available adverse-media sources. Every UBO, general partner, director, officer, and signatory must be screened. Foreign and domestic PEP status must be determined, and enhanced due diligence must apply if any PEP, sanction, or negative-media hit is identified. Screening must be repeated at onboarding and re-run within 24 hours of any material sanctions-list update or change of UBO.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Quebec Enterprise Registrar — Registraire des entreprises (https://www.registrairedesentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names in Quebec must be expressed in French. The primary name must contain a French lexical unit or a recognized distinct token accompanied by a French generic. Non-Latin scripts are not accepted; Latin-script transliteration is required. The legal-form suffix must be the French 'société en commandite' or abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; English 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP' is not an acceptable legal element in the registered name. A registered foreign trademark may be used as a distinct token if the rest of the name is in French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises refuses the proposed name, the filer may submit a written request for reconsideration within 30 days of the refusal, together with a revised name proposal and any supporting explanations, through the Registraire's secure online portal. If the reconsideration is rejected, the filer may apply for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c. C-25.01. The court application must be filed within 60 days of the refusal decision or reconsideration decision, as applicable, and notice of the application must be served on the Attorney General of Quebec and the Registraire des enterprises.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A limited partnership must maintain a physical registered office address in Quebec where notices and legal process may be served and statutory records are kept. A virtual office is permissible only where the service provider maintains a genuine commercial physical location in Quebec under a written service agreement for the Receipt of process and safe custody of corporate records. A pure letterbox arrangement with no service-of-process capability or recordkeeping function is not acceptable. For an ISIC 6201 remote software business, a serviced office or law-firm address satisfies the ordinary commercial substance requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified at approximately 5% over a three-year period for a standard software/SAAS entity with no statutory license requirement. The Registraire des entreprises, FINTRAC, CRA, and Revenu Quebec may conduct unannounced visits only on reasonable grounds, upon complaint, or during an audit, and no mandatory periodic physical inspection is scheduled.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2236 and 2240-2246 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 6, 17, 21-32 and its fee regulation (declaration of registration and publication in the Gazette officielle du Québec).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), the statutory registry authority under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; online portal: registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation), form RE-200 or the online portal equivalent, filed under section 17 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, followed by statutory publication in the Gazette officielle du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Quebec limited partnership; capital contributions are fixed contractually in the Partnership Agreement and no escrow, deposit guarantee, or capital verification is mandated for an ISIC 6201 software-services business. Limited partners may contribute cash, assets, or services, but a limited partner who engages in management activity loses the liability shield under art. 2246 C.c.Q.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Limited Partnership adopts the Partnership Agreement as executed and initialed, and accepts the capital subscriptions of the Limited Partners as set out in Schedule A, crediting their capital accounts accordingly; RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal establishment of the Partnership shall be located at [registered address], Montréal, Québec, and that [General Partner] is designated as managing partner with full authority to bind the Partnership; RESOLVED, that the compliance officer is appointed to maintain the register of partners, file the declaration of registration and annual updates with the Registraire des entreprises, and execute all governance documents; RESOLVED, that the banking, tax-registration, and licensing instructions are hereby ratified.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online service, My Business Account, and Represent a Client portals; and Revenu Quebec, including the clicSÉQUR and online tax-services portals for Quebec tax accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Quebec limited partnership or foreign partnership carrying on business, earning income, employing personnel, or having a Canadian tax filing obligation should obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online or the CRA non-resident registration process. The entity must add the applicable program accounts, including GST/HST (RT), payroll deductions (RP), and, where applicable, corporation income tax or information-reporting accounts. A partnership may also have to file a T5013 Partnership Information Return, generally using the partnership's BN. For Quebec operations, the entity should register with Revenu Quebec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), payroll source deductions, and other applicable accounts. Registration is generally completed using the entity's formation or partnership documents, principal business and Canadian activity details, responsible-person information, ownership and partner information, authorization documents, and non-resident contact details. A non-resident supplier may use the CRA simplified GST/HST registration regime for qualifying digital-economy supplies to Canadian consumers, but that regime does not generally replace full GST/HST registration where the supplier is carrying on business in Canada or making supplies requiring the regular regime. A QST registration may similarly be required under Quebec's specified digital economy rules or the general QST regime. A Canadian BN, GST/HST account, and QST number are separate from a Quebec enterprise number issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian limited partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income-tax purposes: partnership income or loss is calculated at the partnership level and allocated to partners under the partnership agreement and Canadian tax rules, with partners generally taxed on their allocated shares. Canada has no general US-style check-the-box election that converts a Canadian limited partnership into a corporation or disregarded entity for Canadian tax purposes. A partnership may use specific statutory elections where conditions are met, including rollover elections under section 97 of the Income Tax Act for qualifying transfers of property to a partnership, partnership-level and partner-level elections under applicable tax provisions, and elections concerning the tax treatment of certain financial or depreciable property. A qualifying partnership may also be eligible for limited partnership loss rules, foreign-affiliate and treaty-based positions, or other specialized regimes, subject to statutory conditions. Canadian anti-hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or alter income inclusions for arrangements involving foreign entities or instruments treated inconsistently across jurisdictions; these rules are not elective entity-classification elections. US tax classification is determined under US law and does not change the Canadian legal or default tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) applying in participating provinces; Quebec separately imposes the Quebec Sales Tax (QST). Quebec generally applies GST at 5% and QST at 9.975% to taxable supplies, subject to place-of-supply, zero-rating, exemptions, and special non-resident digital-economy rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, determined under the applicable GST/HST small-supplier rules, generally measured over the relevant preceding or immediately following four-quarter period. QST registration generally applies at the corresponding CAD 30,000 threshold for taxable supplies, subject to Quebec rules and specified digital-economy provisions. The threshold is not a general exemption where the supplier voluntarily registers or is otherwise required to register because of Canadian business activities, non-resident digital-economy rules, or other statutory nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not generally impose a universal real-time electronic invoicing or pre-clearance mandate for ordinary B2B or B2C software supplies. GST/QST invoices must contain prescribed information when required, including supplier identity and registration numbers, supply description, consideration, applicable tax rates, and tax amounts. Electronic invoices and records are generally acceptable if they preserve reliability, integrity, accessibility, and auditability. CRA and Revenu Quebec may require electronic filing for specified returns, remittances, information returns, and payroll obligations, but these requirements do not constitute real-time fiscal clearance. A supplier using Stripe, Paddle, or another merchant-of-record arrangement must establish whether it or the merchant is the legal supplier, importer, or tax collector and must retain transaction, customer-location, tax-rate, exemption, refund, and payment records. No general digital tax stamp is required for the stated software activity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For GST purposes, exported goods may generally be zero-rated where they are supplied for export and the statutory export conditions are satisfied, including export from Canada within the applicable time and evidence that the goods were exported. Services supplied to a non-resident may generally be zero-rated where the recipient is non-resident and the service is not excluded by the place-of-supply and exported-service exceptions. Software access, remote-support software, cloud functionality, and telemetry services require an analysis of the legal nature of the supply, customer residence, user location, performance location, contractual rights, and whether the service relates to real property, tangible personal property, or services performed in Canada. A non-resident customer alone does not automatically establish zero-rating. Supplies made to or for a Canadian resident, or supplies used or consumed in Canada, may be taxable. QST zero-rating and exemption rules must be analyzed separately under Quebec legislation. Registered businesses may generally claim input tax credits for eligible GST/HST paid and input tax refunds or credits for eligible QST paid, subject to documentary support, business-use requirements, restrictions, and filing compliance. A non-resident digital supplier using a simplified registration generally has restricted input-tax recovery compared with a registrant under the regular regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian export declaration or applicable Canada Border Services Agency export reporting record for goods where an export declaration is required
Commercial invoice, purchase order, contract, and packing list identifying the supplier, purchaser, goods, value, destination, and export terms
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier evidence showing export from Canada
Proof of delivery or importation in the destination jurisdiction, where relevant
Customer-residency and contractual evidence for exported services, including customer address, tax status, service description, user-location evidence, and records supporting non-resident status
Bank, payment-processor, and settlement records supporting consideration received; an inward-remittance certificate is not a general Canadian statutory requirement
GST/HST and QST invoices, credit notes, refund records, and accounting ledgers supporting the zero-rated or exported supply
Customs documents are generally not applicable to electronically delivered software or services with no export of tangible goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general foreign-exchange repatriation requirement or mandatory 180-day remittance deadline for export proceeds. CRA and Revenu Quebec may audit the transaction, deny zero-rating, reassess GST/HST or QST, assess interest, and recover improperly claimed input tax credits or refunds where export, customer-residency, place-of-supply, or documentary conditions are not proven. Tax may be reassessed for the statutory reassessment period and for an unlimited period in cases of misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful blindness, or fraud. False statements and omissions may attract statutory penalties, including gross-negligence or other prescribed penalties, in addition to tax and interest. Failure to register, collect, remit, file, or maintain records may result in separate administrative penalties. Deliberate tax evasion, fraud, obstruction, or use of false documents may result in prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. A fraudulent zero-rating claim may also trigger denial of refunds, recovery of amounts already paid, audit expansion to related supplies, and partner-level or director-level exposure where applicable under Canadian law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada / Banque du Canada (monetary authority and retail payment supervision), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation of banks and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CFT supervision. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control authority because the historical Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts without surrender, conversion, or remittance-approval requirements. Profit repatriation to foreign limited partners is unrestricted at the exchange-control level: a non-resident partner carrying on business in Canada is taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on its allocated partnership income, and routine distributions of allocated income are not subject to Part XIII gross withholding. However, payments of interest, royalties, rent, or management fees to non-resident partners attract 25% Part XIII withholding subject to treaty relief. Practical compliance gates are FATCA/CRS self-certification, FINTRAC transaction reports for cash or large virtual currency transactions at or above CAD 10,000, and Form T1135 foreign property reporting by resident partners whose specified foreign property cost exceeds CAD 100,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or forced repatriation of export proceeds. Software export receipts for remote desktop access and unattended IoT telemetry licensing are zero-rated for GST/HST purposes as zero-rated supplies of digital goods and services. Foreign-currency receivables may be retained, swept, and hedged freely; the only obligations are ordinary CRA and Revenu Québec record-keeping, accurate reporting of partnership income, and foreign-source disclosure where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada / Banque Nationale du Canada
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (CAD/USD)
Operational Account (CAD; optional USD Borderless Plan)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a supplementary collection and disbursement rail; NOT acceptable as the primary banking layer. Foreign digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, and Stripe Treasury embedded accounts can legally support multi-currency collections and vendor payouts, but any provider serving Canadian users must be registered or be in the transitional registration window under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with the Bank of Canada. EMIs do not provide CDIC deposit insurance, credit facilities, or Quebec provincial regulatory comfort. The LP must therefore maintain its principal operating and capital accounts with a Schedule I bank and use EMIs only to optimize cross-currency conversion, merchant payouts, and last-mile vendor payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for in-person branch appearance. Canadian Schedule I banks and Desjardins permit fully remote onboarding of a Quebec-registered limited partnership using video KYC, provided the general partner or its appointed officer is a Canadian resident individual with verifiable identity, the partnership is registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ), and the CRA business number and GST/QST account registrations are presented. A physical branch visit may be requested only on exception, such as where all ultimate beneficial owners are non-resident or source-of-wealth files are incomplete. Quebec linguistic rules require standard-form banking agreements to be available in French; bilingual onboarding files should be prepared in advance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque limited-partner chain or unidentified ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete partnership agreement and partnership register; organizational chart disclosing the general partner and all limited partners; certified registration extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ); UBO identification with passport and proof of residential address; source of funds and source of wealth attestations for each capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners and cross-border wire profile with no physical commercial footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRS/FATCA self-certification forms and tax-residency certificates for all non-resident partners; revenue model evidence including SaaS licensing agreements, merchant-of-record contracts with Stripe and Paddle, and subscription billing records; PIPEDA-compliant privacy policy and technology stack documentation demonstrating active Canadian operations; five-year business plan with cash-flow projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value merchant settlements that structurally mimic transaction structuring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Paddle merchant agreements and settlement statements; automated ledger reconciliation mapping gateway payouts to deferred revenue schedules; customer invoices and payment method data; explanatory memorandum for FINTRAC describing the recurring digital-subscription business model and daily payout cadence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proceeds originating from remote-IoT or telemetry-related customers in higher-risk jurisdictions or ambiguous end users
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export control and trade compliance self-assessment confirming no controlled-good classification (ECCN or CCL N/A) for the telemetry software; end-user and end-use declarations; remote-access software security documentation including SOC 2 or ISO 27001 reports; data-residency statements for deployed IoT installations; written IT security attestation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner contributions must enter as SWIFT MT103 wires credited through the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) to the LP Schedule I bank account. Wire instructions require the receiving bank SWIFT/BIC, Canadian institution number, transit number, account number, and beneficiary legal name exactly as registered in Quebec. The payment reference field should state 'Capital contribution - Partnership Agreement dated [date]'. A contribution ledger, executed capital call resolution, and source-of-funds evidence must be pre-positioned so the credit is verified against the capital account before deployment. For US-dollar contributions routed from US partners, settle via Fedwire or CHIPS to the bank US correspondent, converting to CAD at a pre-agreed rate or holding USD in a designated sub-account. All inbound wires must be screened against FINTRAC reporting thresholds and Canadian sanctions lists.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Customer collections are settled by Stripe and Paddle as merchant-of-record payouts through ACH, SEPA, and local clearing rails into the LP operational account on a standard T+2 cycle; this is the primary revenue clearing rail. Vendor payments and non-resident partner distributions clear via SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wires or Canadian EFT and LVTS for domestic payments. For hardware-integrated IoT components, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit under UCP600 is available but operationally unnecessary for a zero-inventory software business. Distributions to non-resident partners must be supported by accurate T5013 and RL-15 filings, with Part XIII withholding applied separately to any interest, royalty, rent, or management fee components embedded in the distribution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable USD/CAD FX forward contracts with a Schedule I Canadian bank counterparty
Over-the-counter vanilla FX options on USD/CAD for subscription revenue downside protection
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD) matched to specific capital contribution or receivable maturities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited strictly to settlement of non-convertible or restricted-currency exposures arising from partner or customer funds outside the G10
Foreign-currency demand deposits and automatic sweep arrangements rather than speculative derivative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Registration (Déclaration annuelle) pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual anniversary rule: within 60 days after each anniversary date of the initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee and interest charged by REQ; fines under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; after prior notice, administrative strike-off (radiation) of the LP registration and cancellation of the enterprise number (NEQ) if the declaration remains unfiled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal income tax information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the LP fiscal period; for a December 31 fiscal period end, on or before March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day for each day the return is late, capped at CAD 2,500 per partnership; partners relying on unfiled T5013 amounts may be assessed with arrears interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Information Return (Québec provincial income tax information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the LP fiscal period (June 30 for a December 31 fiscal period end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and omission penalties plus interest under the Taxation Act (Québec); partners provincial income allocations may be recomputed and formal demands issued.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No Quebec statutory audit is compulsory for a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A full independent audit is triggered only when: (a) the LP becomes a reporting issuer under securities legislation; (b) a court or regulator requires it; (c) the partnership agreement or lender covenants require an audit; or (d) the LP exceeds a review-engagement threshold imposed by its own constituent documents. For non-reporting LPs, a review engagement (CSRE 2400) is the market standard.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements for a Canadian private enterprise LP follow IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) or ASPE (Part II); ASPE is the usual framework for a non-public LP. The T5013 and TP-600 schedules are prepared from tax-basis accounts reconciled to the financial statements; the underlying accounting records must support reported partnership income allocations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a standalone annual UBO declaration for a limited partnership. The REQ annual declaration re-confirms the registered general partner (registrant) and primary business information; any transfer of partnership interests or change in general partner particulars must be declared to REQ within 60 days of the change. The federal Canada Business Corporations Act significant-control register applies only to CBCA corporations, and no equivalent provincial register currently applies to a Quebec LP; the LP nevertheless documents each partner identity, contribution, and profit share in the register of partners and records transfers in the partnership decision log.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners and Capital Contributions
General Partner Resolution and Decision Log (Minute Book)
REQ Registration and Annual Declaration File (legal publicity file)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-750 per annum for a Quebec registered office and registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000-15,000 per annum (review engagement USD 3,000-6,500; full audit USD 6,500-15,000 for a small private LP)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15%) and Quebec (11.5%) corporate tax rate; not levied at LP entity level due to flow-through taxation
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credits (up to 35% refundable for qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations) and Quebec R&D tax credits (up to 30% refundable); reduced small-business corporate rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income applies only to corporate partners, not to the limited partnership itself

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return, filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via EFAST/e-file or a CRA-approved tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than the last day of the fifth month after the end of the partnership's fiscal period (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, due May 31).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the limited partnership, business number, registered office address (Quebec), jurisdiction of formation (Quebec), fiscal period start and end dates, and general partner name/address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a limited partnership with non-resident partners, confirm the foreign partner's name, permanent establishment status, and country of residence; a local business number in Quebec is required for the partnership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code using NAICS 511210 (Software Publishers), ISIC 6201 (Computer Programming Consultancies), and description of remote desktop access and unattended machine telemetry software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State that commercial activity is online software licensing; there is no physical installation or statutory license required in Quebec. Ensure the description matches the transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income, loss, tax credits, and specified deductions to each partner, including percentage allocation, Canadian tax number of resident partners, and non-resident partner identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate active business income to non-resident partners on a net basis under Part I of the Income Tax Act. File the corresponding T5013 Summary and RLO RL-15; do not treat profit allocations as dividends.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 (per return); knowingly making a false or misleading statement attracts a penalty of up to CAD 25,000. CRA may also impose a due-diligence penalty of 10% of unreported income for non-arm's-length transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Relevé 15 (RL-15) – Income from a Partnership, filed with Revenu Quebec via CLICK.us/Familink or authorized commercial software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed with Revenu Quebec on or before the same deadline as the federal T5013 return (last day of the fifth month after the fiscal period-end); partner copies must be provided by the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full name, address, Quebec business/tax number, and partnership percentage share for each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners without a Quebec business number, use the federal business number and attach a note to the RL-15 indicating the partner's foreign tax domicile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share of the partnership's net business income/loss, capital gains/losses, and any amount that is exempt from Quebec income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only the income that is reasonably attributable to the partnership's business carried on in Quebec; claim treaty protection under the Canada-Quebec agreement if the income is effectively connected to a Quebec permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report any amounts related to remote support software including subscription fees, license royalties, and IoT telemetry data servicing charges, if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separately identify cross-border royalty amounts that may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax to avoid double reporting in the partnership's ordinary income allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount determined to be payable, plus 1% for each full month late (up to 12 months); failure to issue RL-15 to a partner may result in a penalty of CAD 100 per slip, and wilful omission can lead to a penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act for dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident; for distributions of a limited partnership, profit allocations to non-resident partners are not dividends. Such allocations are subject to Part I net-basis taxation at graduated rates, and no Part XIII withholding tax applies to active business income of the partnership if the non-resident partner files a Canadian return and is entitled to treaty protection.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced treaty rates on any Canadian-source withholding payments (interest, royalties, dividends), the non-resident partner must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction to the partnership/payor before payment. The payor applies the reduced rate at source; if the statutory rate was withheld, the non-resident must file CRA Form NR7 (Application by a Non-Resident for a Refund of a Part XIII Withholding Tax) or a T2/T5013 adjustment, together with supporting treaty documentation and the TRC. For Quebec, an additional RL-19 return or a refund application to Revenu Quebec is required where provincial proportionate withholding applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding; reduced to 10% (usually 10-15%) through tax treaties (e.g., Canada-US treaty Article XII). For computer software source royalties and IoT telemetry licensing, treaty benefits require both economic entitlement and residence proof. Interest: 25% statutory; treaties often reduce to between 0% and 15%; arm's-length cross-border interest paid by a Canadian resident may be exempt under specific domestic provisions. For an LP, any such withholding is computed on the payment by the entity, but remains the liability of the non-resident recipient absent a valid TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: T106 reporting is mandatory for cross-border non-arm's-length transactions if the aggregate fair market value exceeds CAD 1,000,000. Comprehensive Canadian transfer-pricing documentation (Local File) is expected by CRA where controlled transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000; a Master File and Country-by-Country report are generally required once consolidated group revenue reaches CAD 750,000,000 (roughly aligned with the OECD EUR 750 million threshold).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the Gulf-cooperation style; however, the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under subsection 245(2) and the statutory transfer-pricing rules under section 247 require that transactions be commercially rational and that profits be allocated according to economic substance, functions performed, assets used, and risks assumed. A Quebec limited partnership with no employees, no office, and no business activity in Quebec will be disregarded or re-characterized; the CRA may assess the non-resident general partner directly and deny the flow-through status. For remote screen share and IoT software, the partnership must demonstrate real personnel, decision-making, and support operations in Quebec, or the income source and beneficial ownership will be re-attributed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly or negligently making false or misleading statements in T5013 or RL-15, understating non-resident partner income, omitting cross-border royalty revenue from Stripe/Paddle, or failing to report IoT telemetry service income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under subsection 239(1) of the Income Tax Act for tax evasion carries a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment; civil penalty under subsection 163(2) is equal to 50% of the gross understatement (reduced to 25% where the filing was made based on adequate disclosure). Revenu Quebec imposes the same penalties for provincial evasion, with additional late-interest accumulation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners of the LP are personally and jointly and severally liable for the partnership's tax and penalties; officers/directors of a corporate general partner may be assessed personally under subsection 226(1) for unremitted amounts and can face travel restrictions, asset-freezing orders, and restraint orders in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Quebec LP with no economic substance, no employees, no Quebec address, or a circular ownership structure designed to shift profits to no-tax jurisdictions; issuing false invoices to foreign partners for remote support or telemetry data services not actually performed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under GAAR, the CRA may deny tax benefits and reassess the partnership for the full amount plus interest; a penalty under subsection 245(4) of 25% of the tax benefit is applied unless a reasonable justification is shown. Revenu Quebec may disallow the LP's Quebec nexus and impose a 100% diligence penalty for failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner may be subject to a court order for restitution if they authorized the sham arrangement; personal liability can arise under contract law, corporate law, or the Quebec Tax Administration Act for allowing the partnership to operate without honest commercial purpose. In egregious cases, an Order for a travel permit may be required before an individual may leave Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting subscription payments through Stripe or Paddle from persons/businesses using remote screen share software to access devices without consent, or failing to file a suspicious transaction report if software telemetry is used in illegal activity; failing to verify beneficial owners (UBOs) of the LP.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) imposes administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000,000 for an entity; a criminal offence can lead to a fine of up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for a person; directors/officers can be charged independently for failing to maintain an AML compliance program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate officers/directors can be criminally prosecuted under the PCMLTFA for knowingly directing, authorizing, or acquiescing in the offence; they may be subject to a personal administrative penalty of up to CAD 500,000 and a court-ordered travel ban if they attempt to leave Canada while charges are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or produce contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border non-arm's-length transactions (e.g., licensing of software source code, telemetry data, or services to a foreign partner), and failing to file T106 while exceeding the CAD 1,000,000 aggregate threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA will adjust the consideration to arm's length and assess taxes on the upward profit adjustment; the penalty under subsection 247(5) is 10% of the amount of gross adjustment (without reference to net tax, and without deduction for offsetting adjustments) for each year in which the taxpayer failed to make reasonable efforts at documentation. Interest is compounded daily and no penalty relief is available for the statutory 10% unless the taxpayer proves due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors, officers, and agents of the corporate general partner who knowingly or negligently caused the failure to document are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties to the extent they participated in the decision; they may be assessed personally under Quebec's civil lift-the-corporate-veil doctrine if the LP is insolvent and the transaction was a sham.
